sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Graphs model real-world networks: social connections, city routes, task dependencies, and internet topology. Graph interviews test both algorithmic ability (BFS/DFS) and system thinking (cycle detection = deadlock, topological sort = build order). Every fresher is expected to solve Number of Islands and detect cycles in a graph.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Graph = vertices + edges**. Represent as adjacency list: `Map<Integer, List<Integer>>` or `List<List<Integer>>`.
- **BFS**: Use a Queue + visited set. Level-by-level — finds shortest path in unweighted graphs.
- **DFS**: Use recursion or Stack + visited set. Explores depth-first — finds cycles, connected components.
- **Cycle detection (directed)**: Track 3 states per node — UNVISITED, IN_PROGRESS (in current DFS path), DONE. Back edge to IN_PROGRESS = cycle.
- **Cycle detection (undirected)**: Track parent — if neighbor is visited and is not parent, cycle exists.
- **Topological sort**: Only for DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph). Output: nodes ordered such that all edges go from earlier to later.
- **Grid as graph**: Each cell is a node; neighbors are up/down/left/right.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **graph-representations**: Adjacency list is O(V+E) space — preferred unless dense graph (then adjacency matrix).
- **bfs-traversal**: Add start to queue + visited; while queue not empty: dequeue, add unvisited neighbors to queue + visited.
- **dfs-traversal**: Recursive DFS: mark visited, then recurse on all unvisited neighbors.
- **cycle-detection**: Directed graph uses coloring (0=white, 1=gray, 2=black); undirected tracks parent.
- **topological-sort**: Kahn's algorithm: compute in-degrees, add 0-in-degree nodes to queue, process and reduce in-degrees.
- **number-of-islands**: Flood fill DFS — when land cell found, DFS marks the whole island as visited.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"How do you represent a graph in Java?"* — Adjacency list using Map<Integer, List<Integer>> or List<List<Integer>>.
- *"How do BFS and DFS differ?"* — BFS explores level-by-level (queue), finds shortest path; DFS explores depth-first (stack/recursion).
- *"How do you solve Number of Islands?"* — For each '1' cell, DFS marks the entire connected island as visited; count DFS calls.
- *"How do you detect a cycle in a directed graph?"* — 3-color DFS: cycle exists when you reach a GRAY (in current path) node.
- *"What is topological sort?"* — Linear ordering of DAG nodes such that for every edge u→v, u comes before v.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'll model this as a graph problem: [describe vertices and edges], then apply [BFS/DFS/topological sort] with a visited array to avoid revisiting nodes, giving O(V+E) time complexity."*
